content.title: About
content.content: Pupusa is a traditional Salvadoran dish consisting of a thin corn‑maize tortilla filled with seasoned meat and beans. The dough, made from masa (finely ground corn flour), is cooked until soft yet sturdy, creating a pocket that holds the savory filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pupusas are often served with curtido (pickled cabbage) and salsa roja, which add tangy contrast.
Traditionally they are cooked on a flat griddle called a “comal” over an open flame.
In El Salvador, pupusas are a national staple and are featured in festivals and family gatherings.
There are many filling variations, from cheese and spinach to seafood; meat with beans is one of the most popular.
The corn masa provides complex carbohydrates that give lasting energy.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat filling supplies high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Beans and corn masa add soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and beans provide B6, B12, and folate, which are important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish offers iron, zinc, and magnesium, contributing to immune health and energy production.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Pupusas are naturally low in sugar, making them suitable for balanced carbohydrate intake.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to corn masa used in the tortilla.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: If the filling is seasoned with salty sauces, the dish can be high in sodium.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Meat‑and‑bean pupusas are relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor harmful bacteria; ensure the filling reaches a safe internal temperature.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pupusas are served hot, usually split in half. Eat them with your hands, topping with salsa, sour cream, grated cheese, or avocado. For a fresher bite, add sliced tomatoes, lettuce, or pickled onions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pupusas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. They can be frozen wrapped tightly in plastic and later reheated on a skillet or in the microwave.
